findings.summary: Token resolution happens in two independent paths: sync-command.ts pre-resolves via resolveGitHubToken, and AuthOptionsBuilder has its own fallback resolution
evidence: sync-command.ts:341-351: resolveGitHubToken called with process.env.GH_TOKEN, result passed as repoToken to processor
auth-options-builder.ts:25-27: if preResolvedToken !== undefined, uses it directly; otherwise falls back to its own resolveGitHubToken call at line 30
ProcessorOptions.token docstring: 'Pre-resolved GitHub token -- avoids duplicate resolution in AuthOptionsBuilder'
findings.suggestion: Choose one resolution site. Either always pre-resolve in sync-command (and make AuthOptionsBuilder only build auth options from a required token), or let AuthOptionsBuilder own all resolution and remove pre-resolution from sync-command.

findings.summary: Several boundary handoffs pass wide options bags (10+ fields) that bundle per-call context with stable config, making the integration seam hard to reason about
evidence: CommitPushOptions has 11 fields: repoInfo, gitOps, workDir, fileChanges, commitMessage, pushBranch, isDirectMode, dryRun, retries, token, executor
BranchSetupOptions has 10 fields: repoInfo, branchName, baseBranch, workDir, isDirectMode, dryRun, retries, token, gitOps, executor
SyncWorkflow.execute spreads these across multiple call sites, re-destructuring the same fields
findings.suggestion: Group stable per-session context (repoInfo, workDir, dryRun, retries, token, executor) into a shared context object passed through the workflow, keeping per-step options minimal.

findings.summary: process.env access for GH_TOKEN occurs in repository-processor.ts (composition root) and commit-strategy-selector.ts (library code), violating the DI boundary
evidence: repository-processor.ts:81: new AuthOptionsBuilder(tokenManager, logInstance, process.env.GH_TOKEN) -- acceptable as composition root
commit-strategy-selector.ts:14: process.env.XFG_GITHUB_APP_ID && process.env.XFG_GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY -- library function reads env directly
commit-strategy-selector.ts:26-27: process.env.XFG_GITHUB_APP_ID!, process.env.XFG_GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY! -- passed to constructor from env in library code
findings.suggestion: Inject app credentials into createTokenManager/getCommitStrategy as parameters rather than reading process.env in library code. The composition root (repository-processor.ts or sync-command.ts) should be the only env reader.

findings.summary: PR and commit strategies are created fresh via factory functions at each call site rather than being injected, creating implicit coupling at integration seams
evidence: branch-manager.ts:34: const strategy = getPRStrategy(repoInfo, executor, this.log) -- creates strategy inline during setupBranch
commit-push-manager.ts:49: const commitStrategy = getCommitStrategy(repoInfo, executor) -- creates strategy inline during commitAndPush
pr-creator.ts:173: const strategy = getPRStrategy(repoInfo, executor, log) -- creates strategy inline in createPR function
findings.suggestion: Inject strategy factories via constructor so the seam is explicit and testable without mocking module-level functions.

findings.summary: sync-command.ts mixes CLI concern (option parsing, logging) with orchestration (lifecycle, file sync, settings, reporting), making the integration seam between CLI and domain unclear
evidence: sync-command.ts has 601 lines with 7 top-level functions: processSingleRepo, runLifecyclePhase, runFileSyncPhase, applyRepoSettings, displayReports, logSettingsResult, runSync
RepoIterationContext (line 269-288) bundles 13 fields of mixed concern: CLI options, domain processors, report collectors
runSync at line 524 does config loading, validation, normalization, branch naming, processor creation, lifecycle manager creation, iteration, and reporting
findings.suggestion: Extract a SyncOrchestrator class that owns the per-repo iteration loop (lifecycle -> sync -> settings -> collect), leaving sync-command.ts as a thin CLI adapter that parses options, creates the orchestrator, and displays results.

findings.summary: Error handling across module boundaries uses inconsistent patterns: some boundaries return result objects with success:false, others throw, and some do both
evidence: CommitPushManager catches errors and returns { success: false, errorResult } (line 66-68), never throws
IPRStrategy.create docstring says 'Throws on infrastructure failures' while merge 'Returns MergeResult for all outcomes including failures. May throw on unexpected infrastructure errors'
sync-command.ts runFileSyncPhase wraps processor.process in try-catch (line 513), but the processor itself also catches internally via SyncWorkflow
findings.suggestion: Standardize: domain boundaries (SyncWorkflow, processors) should always return result objects and never throw for expected failures. Reserve throws for programming errors only. Document this contract consistently.
